attackLog.incidentOrCve: SAP NetWeaver / Web Dispatcher Maximum Severity Flaws (ICM2SHELL & PROXYGATE)
attackLog.target: SAP NetWeaver Application Server, Web Dispatcher, and Gateway software
attackLog.attackVector: Unauthenticated remote code execution via exposed SAP management interfaces without requiring user credentials.
attackLog.immediateSolution: Apply SAP's November 2026 security patches immediately and restrict external access to NetWeaver management ports.

attackLog.attackVector: Active exploitation of recently patched ESG vulnerabilities allowing remote attackers to run arbitrary commands with root privileges.
attackLog.immediateSolution: Verify firmware update implementation and check appliance logs for unauthorized root command execution.

attackLog.target: Microsoft Exchange Servers at government organizations
attackLog.attackVector: State-sponsored threat actors deploying the modular Cereal toolset to silently intercept and steal emails from compromised Exchange servers.
attackLog.immediateSolution: Audit Exchange server extensions, inspect IIS logs for anomalous paths, and deploy updated EDR rules targeting Cereal artifacts.

attackLog.target: Apple iOS 26 and iOS 27 running on iPhones
attackLog.attackVector: Malicious applications leveraging a public sandbox escape (worse_query) to read sensitive files, seed phrases, and private keys from other apps.
attackLog.immediateSolution: Avoid sideloading applications, restrict app permissions, and monitor for pending Apple patches addressing the sandbox flaw.

attackLog.target: Refrigeration controllers at ~700 French retail sites
attackLog.attackVector: Unauthorized remote access to industrial refrigeration controllers resulting in modified defrost settings, food loss, and physical fires.
attackLog.immediateSolution: Isolate OT management interfaces from the corporate network, enforce strict MFA, and audit controller access logs.

attackLog.attackVector: Active in-the-wild exploitation of the eighth Chrome zero-day vulnerability of the year via crafted web pages.
attackLog.immediateSolution: Update Google Chrome immediately to the latest patched version across all endpoints.

attackLog.target: Linux desktop environments utilizing Anthropic's Claude document processing tool
attackLog.attackVector: Attackers construct temporary files processed by Claude's document-processing feature that execute malicious code on host Linux machines.
attackLog.immediateSolution: Restrict AI tool document processing capabilities and apply vendor-supplied updates or input validation controls.

attackLog.target: Vanderbilt University enterprise databases and IT infrastructure
attackLog.attackVector: BYOD ransomware gang infiltrating network endpoints to encrypt databases and exfiltrate sensitive student, employee, and research data.
attackLog.immediateSolution: Activate incident response plan, isolate impacted BYOD endpoints, and engage forensic investigators.

deepDives.title: SAP NetWeaver Maximum Severity Flaws: ICM2SHELL and PROXYGATE Exploitation Analysis
deepDives.whatHappened: SAP released its November 2026 security bulletin featuring four CVSS 10.0 vulnerabilities affecting NetWeaver and Web Dispatcher software. These flaws allow unauthenticated remote code execution across core enterprise resource planning platforms.
deepDives.technicalMechanism: The ICM2SHELL and PROXYGATE flaws exploit improper handling of incoming web requests and internal communication channels within the NetWeaver application server and Web Dispatcher components. Attackers can bypass authentication layers to execute arbitrary system commands with high privileges.
deepDives.asciiFlow: [External Attacker] ──► (HTTP Request / Crafted Payload) ──► [SAP Web Dispatcher] ──► [NetWeaver Server (ICM2SHELL)] ──► [Root/System Execution]
remediation: Apply SAP November 2026 Support Package Stacks / Patches immediately.
Implement strict network perimeter filtering to block direct access to SAP ICM and Gateway ports from untrusted zones.
Monitor SAP audit logs for unauthorized administrative actions and anomalous RFC connection attempts.
deepDives.lessonsLearned: Core enterprise middleware remains a primary vector for unauthenticated RCE. Organizations must decouple internal management interfaces from internet-facing architectures via zero-trust network access (ZTNA) policies.

deepDives.title: Turla's Modular Cereal Malware Targeting Government Exchange Servers
deepDives.whatHappened: The Russian state-sponsored threat group Turla (Snake) was uncovered utilizing a newly documented, modular espionage toolset named 'Cereal' to silently intercept and exfiltrate emails from Microsoft Exchange servers at targeted government entities.
deepDives.technicalMechanism: Cereal deploys as a sophisticated post-exploitation framework that integrates directly into Microsoft Exchange architecture. It hooks into message transport and storage pipelines, enabling stealthy data collection without triggering standard endpoint alerts.
deepDives.asciiFlow: [Turla Operator] ──► [Compromised Exchange Edge/CAS] ──► [Cereal Module Hooks] ──► [Silent Mailbox Exfiltration]
remediation: Conduct comprehensive forensic hunts across all Microsoft Exchange environments for unauthorized transport agent modifications.
Update EDR and SIEM detection signatures to identify Cereal-specific behavioral artifacts and anomalous IIS worker process activities.
Enforce multi-factor authentication and rigorous administrative auditing across all mail server infrastructures.
deepDives.lessonsLearned: Advanced persistent threat (APT) groups continually refine modular toolsets to blend in with legitimate administrative traffic. Rich network telemetry and out-of-band monitoring are vital to detecting post-exploitation persistence.

deepDives.title: IRGC State-Sponsored Sabotage of French Retail Refrigeration Controllers
deepDives.cve: MITRE ATT&CK: T0831 (Manipulation of Control View) / T1489
deepDives.whatHappened: The French government formally attributed an October cyberattack targeting refrigeration controllers across ~700 retail sites to a cyber unit of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). Attackers altered defrost settings to dangerous levels, causing food spoilage and physical fires.
deepDives.technicalMechanism: Threat actors exploited insecurely configured remote management interfaces on retail refrigeration controllers, directly modifying operational setpoints. By driving defrost cycles to extreme temperatures, they induced thermal stress, hardware failures, and subsequent physical fires.
deepDives.asciiFlow: [IRGC Cyber Unit] ──► [Exposed Retail Network / VPN] ──► [Refrigeration Controller] ──► [Modified Defrost Setpoints] ──► [Thermal Stress & Physical Fires]
remediation: Immediately audit and disconnect all retail OT/ICS equipment from direct internet exposure.
Implement robust hardware-level logging and boundary firewalls between corporate IT networks and industrial store controllers.
Deploy continuous integrity monitoring on environmental control thresholds to detect automated sabotage attempts.
deepDives.lessonsLearned: The convergence of IT and IoT/OT in retail and commercial environments expands the cyber-physical attack surface. Securing operational equipment requires strict network segmentation and zero-trust remote access controls.

dailyQuestions.scenario: A security analyst is reviewing telemetry following the disclosure of SAP NetWeaver vulnerabilities (ICM2SHELL and PROXYGATE) rated at CVSS 10.0. The flaws allow unauthenticated remote code execution. Which of the following is the most effective immediate operational mitigation before patches can be applied?
options: A) Disable all user accounts across the enterprise domain.
B) Restrict external network access to NetWeaver management and Gateway ports using perimeter firewalls.
C) Enable full disk encryption on all client workstations.
D) Upgrade the corporate antivirus definitions to the latest signature set.
dailyQuestions.rationale: Because the SAP flaws allow unauthenticated remote code execution via internet-facing management interfaces, restricting external network access to those ports at the perimeter firewall is the most effective immediate mitigating control until patches are deployed.

dailyQuestions.scenario: An enterprise is analyzing the Turla 'Cereal' malware campaign which targets Microsoft Exchange servers for silent email interception. As a Principal Security Architect, you are designing a defense-in-depth architecture to detect post-exploitation persistence in messaging infrastructure. Which architectural strategy provides the highest fidelity detection against modular server-side hooks?
options: A) Relying solely on perimeter signature-based antivirus scanning on incoming emails.
B) Implementing file integrity monitoring (FIM) and behavioral telemetry on Exchange transport agents alongside out-of-band network traffic analysis.
C) Enforcing complex user password policies and mandatory annual security awareness training.
D) Migrating all client endpoints to a virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI) environment.
dailyQuestions.rationale: File integrity monitoring (FIM) on transport agents and behavioral telemetry combined with out-of-band network analysis provide deep visibility into server-side persistence mechanisms like Cereal, whereas perimeter AV and user training do not address internal server compromise.

detectionRules.title: Suspicious Process Spawned by Exchange Worker Process (Indicative of Cereal Activity)
detectionRules.code:
title: Suspicious Child Process of Exchange W3WP
status: production
description: Detects unexpected shell execution spawned by Microsoft Exchange worker processes, potentially indicating Turla Cereal malware activity.
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\w3wp.exe'
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate Exchange administrative troubleshooting scripts
level: high
